newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen near session highs on Tankan, awaits data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen near session highs on Tankan, awaits data.

text.p: The dollar was near session peaks against the dollar at midday in Europe as the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) quarterly Tankan report showed only a modest economic recovery and pointed to no change in interest rates.

"There is enough in this survey to confirm that the recovery continues...But it is perhaps less postive than I would have liked with interest rates on hold for the forseeable future," said Daiwa Europe economist Julian Fisher.
The BOJ's quarterly tankan report showed the diffusion index for big manufacturers rose in November to minus three from minus seven in August.

While the headline figure was much in line with forecasts of between minus three to minus two, market sentiment was hit partly because before the tankan survey, Japanese officials had been sounding upbeat on the econmy.
Analysts said the BOJ's forecast of minus one for the key index in March was also cautious and dented sentiment.

Chris Turner, currency strategist at BZW, said while a rate hike was unlikely following the survey, some good news can be rescued from the report. "To describe it as a weak survey is bizarre. Capital spending plans, sales projections and most imortantly, export projections were revised up," he said.
At 1212 GMT dollar/yen was up at 113.30/3.40 against 112.59/69 in late Europee on Tuesday.
"The Tankan is the only thing that has been driving the market this morning. The Japanese bought sterling/yen and dollar/yen on the back of it," said a dealer at a German bank.

Against the mark the dollar was steady at midday at 1.5252/61 against 1.5242/52. Against the Swiss franc the dollar was firm but had lost some of its momentum after powering to 21-month highs of 1.2964 francs on Tuesday.
At 1222 GMT dollar/Swiss stood at 1.2910/20 against 1.2906/16 in late Europe on Tuesday.
Traders said while dollar/Swiss was off its 21-month peaks, it was still firm and helping to lead the dollar.
Jitters over some Swiss banks, perceptions the Swiss franc is still overvalued and a less-than-healthy economy have all helped depress the Swiss franc.
"Dollar/Swiss has come off slighty, but I think it is a pause before a move higher," said the German bank trader.

The dollar could get fresh direction from a raft of economic data due later. The U.S. third-quarter GDP is due at 1330 GMT as is the Q3 price index and jobless claims. The Chicago November PMI and the October durable goods figure come at 1500 GMT.
U.S. third-quarter GDP number is forecast between 1.3- to 2.0-percent growth, with a market consensus at 1.7 percent.
"We are expecting the GDP numbers at 1.6 percent, much in line with the market," said BZW's Turner.
The October durable goods figure and Chicago's November PMI, both due at 1500 GMT, will also be watched closely.
Durable goods orders are forecast to fall between 2.6 and 1.3 percent, with a consensus forecast for a 2.0-percent drop.
